text: Conversion rate types define the category of rate. This lesson covers the day-to-day mechanics: how actual numeric rates get loaded, kept current, and applied when a Spot or Corporate rate is needed.

A daily rate is a specific numeric exchange rate between two currencies, for one rate type, effective on one date. These are managed through Manage Daily Rates, entered manually or loaded through an import process.

Most companies don't type rates in by hand every day. A Daily Rates Import and Calculation process pulls rates from an external feed automatically, keeping Spot and Corporate rates current without manual entry.
Sometimes a direct rate between two currencies isn't available, but rates to a common third currency are. A cross rate rule derives a rate between A and B by routing through that third currency.
Daily rates aren't a set-it-up-once structure — they need fresh data every operating day. Next up, lesson nineteen: opening the first accounting period.
